overview.description: Belote Coinchée (often simply 'La Coinche') is the strategic, bidding-focused evolution of classic Belote. Unlike the standard game where players simply accept or pass a turned card, Coinche involves a full auction where partnerships bid to reach a specific score (e.g., '100 Hearts' or '120 Spades'). The defining mechanic is 'Coincher' (to double) when you believe the opponents cannot make their contract, and 'Surcoincher' (to redouble) if you are confident they can. It is widely considered the most skillful and competitive version of Belote.

history.origins: Evolved from standard Belote in the mid-20th century to satisfy players who wanted more control than the random 'turned card' offered. The bidding system draws inspiration from Bridge.
timeline: 1930s: Early forms like 'Belote aux Enchères' appear.
1950s: The term 'Coinche' (from French slang 'to corner' or 'to nick') solidifies.
Present: The preferred variant for tournaments and serious club play.
history.evolution: Regional variations like 'Contrée' often use slightly different scoring (counting 80, 90, 100...) but the core 'Coinche' mechanic is universal.
history.cultural: A game of bluffs and bold calls. Slapping the table while shouting 'Coinché!' is a dramatic staple of French café culture.

setup.equipment: Standard 32-card French pack (Piquet deck), score pad.
setup.dealing: All 32 cards are dealt at once (usually in batches of 3-2-3). Bidding starts immediately after the deal.

rules.objective: The bidding team must score at least the amount they bid (e.g., 100 points) AND more than the opponents.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid point totals (80 to 160) and a suit. 2. **Doubling**: Opponents can 'Coinche' a bid, doubling its value. 3. **The Play**: Standard Belote rules apply. Must follow suit. Must trump if void (unless partner wins). Must over-trump if possible. 4. **Trump Highs**: Jack (20) and 9 (14) of trumps are the highest cards.
keyRules: You cannot bid lower than the previous bid.
A failed contract (Dedans) results in the defenders scoring all points (162 + melds).
Belote-Rebelote (King and Queen of trumps) scores 20 points regardless of other melds.

strategy.basic: Don't bid 100 unless you have the Jack (Valet) or at least the 9-Ace-10 covered. Remember you need to score 100 POINTS, not just win tricks.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Fit': If your partner bids 80 Hearts and you hold the King and Queen, raise to 100! They likely have the Jack.
strategy.advanced: Bluff Bidding: Bidding a suit you don't have to push opponents higher, or to mislead them about your hand (risky). Also, 'Coinching' on a hunch that they are missing the 9.
tips: Always count your potential points before opening your mouth.
If you have the Jack and 9 of a suit, you effectively own half the deck's value.

list.name: Contrée
list.description: Very similar, often implies that Melds do NOT count towards the contract, or that only 'Capot' (All Tricks) is a valid high bid.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Differences from Coinche are mainly scoring and announcement tweaks that are not yet modeled as engine overrides.

difficulty.easy: Bids strictly on point count. Never Coinches. Plays trumps at random.
difficulty.medium: Recognizes partner raising patterns. Coinches if holding the Jack and Nine of opponents' suit.
difficulty.hard: Advanced bidding signals. Calculates sacrifice bids to minimize losses. Tracks all declarations to map the deck.

considerations: Requires a robust evaluation function for hand-point bidding.
Must implement partnership 'signaling' via leads and discards.

additional: French Federation of Belote (FFB) Official Rules

ante.reason: Belote Coinchée is a point-based partnership game and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante.

deal.reason: The full distribution of eight cards to each of the four players is performed automatically by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: Every card in the 32-card deck is distributed to the players; there is no public market or shared pool.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase or swap cards from any external area; they must succeed with their initial hand.

buy_stock.reason: The entire deck is exhausted during the deal phase; no cards remain in stock to be drawn or purchased.

fold.reason: Players are committed to their partnership's contract and must participate in all eight tricks of the hand.

check.reason: The game uses a trick-taking structure rather than a vying structure where checking would be an appropriate action.

call.reason: There is no pot to match in this game; competition is based on bidding point values and winning tricks.

bet.reason: Success is determined by total point accumulation on a scorecard rather than through the wagering of assets.

raise.reason: Point bids are increased during the auction phase via the bid action rather than through wagering rounds.

declare.description: Declare melds (Tierce, Quarte, Belote) during the first trick.
declare.constraints: Must be leading or playing to the first trick.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private until individual cards are played into tricks; no full-hand reveal phase occurs.

award_pot.reason: Winning points are added to a cumulative session total rather than distributed from a physical pot.

play_card.description: Play a card to the trick; follow suit and trump rules.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit; must trump if void; must over-trump if possible.

draw.reason: All cards are distributed at the start; no drawing phase exists during the play of the tricks.

discard.reason: Every card in the player's hand must be played into a trick; no cards are discarded or buried.

pass.constraints: Allowed during bidding when choosing not to increase the contract.

bid.description: Bid a point value and suit for the contract.
bid.constraints: Must be higher than the current bid.

meld.description: Form a valid sequence or group for bonus points.

go_out.reason: The hand terminates only after all eight tricks have been played by all participants.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: The full hand is dealt at the start; no draw pile exists during the trick-taking play.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played directly to tricks; no separate waste or discard pile is utilized.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Certain ranks (Jack and 9) have high point values in trumps but do not trigger automated actions.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: Auction bidding is performed verbally around the table; no hidden declaration is required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Belote Coinchée is a trick-taking game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Goal is to reach contract score via tricks and melds; hands are played out in tricks, not emptied as in shedding games.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Must over-trump if possible when trumps are played.

customActions.description: Deal eight cards to each player.
Place a contract bid for a specific suit and point total.
Declare a point-scoring sequence during the first trick.
Sum card points and melds to check if contract is met.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; card value comparison determines trick winner (Jack of trumps is highest).
engine.deckDescription: One standard 32-card deck: eight ranks (seven through ace) in each of four suits. No jokers; used for Belote (and Coinche) with bidding, trump, and point values. The jack and nine of trump are the two highest trumps.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (hearts, diamonds, spades, clubs). Trump is determined by the winning bid (or passed to the dealer's choice). Follow suit when able; the jack and nine of trump outrank the ace. Marriage (K-Q of trump) scores bonus.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit. In trump: jack (20), nine (14), ace (11), ten (10), king (4), queen (3), eight and seven (0). In plain suits: ace (11), ten (10), king (4), queen (3), jack (2), nine and eight and seven (0). Belote and coinche use these point values.
engine.dealPattern: Cards are dealt in batches of 3, 2, and 3 cards each.

hero.title: COINCHE
hero.subtitle: Belote aux Enchères
hero.tagline: Bid high. Double down. Don't get caught wet.

synthesis.shortDescription: The high-stakes variant of Belote where players bid on their hands before play begins. With the ability to 'Coinche' (double) opponents, the game becomes a psychological battle of bluffing, calculation, and raw nerve.

prompts.human: The opponents bid '100 Hearts'. You look at your hand: you have the Jack of Spades, Ace of Spades, and the 9 of Hearts (their second best trump!). They can't possibly make 100 points without the 9! Slam the 'COINCHÉ' button!
prompts.ai: Game: Coinche. Type: Bidding/Trick-Taking. Rules: J>9>A>10. Bid target must be reached. Coinche doubles scores. Failing contract gives all points to defenders.

scoring.description: Scores are kept globally. A match is usually to 1000, 2000, or 3000 points.

penalties.Capot: Winning all tricks awards 252 points total.
penalties.Dedans: Bidding team fails contract; defenders get 162 + melds.

scoring.splitRules: Ties are broken by the team that won the last trick (Dix de Der).
